title: Dual-Write Loss and a Transactional Outbox You Can Measure
objective: Implement a service that persists a domain row in PostgreSQL and publishes an event to Kafka, first as two independent writes so a crash drops the event, then as a transactional outbox, and capture both a lost-event run and a zero-loss replay with OpenTelemetry traces spanning commit, poller, and consumer.
whyThisMatters: The SWE saga task asks for compensating steps and idempotency keys. It does not force you to lose an event that your database already committed. That gap — commit succeeded, publish never happened — is the dual-write bug production systems keep rediscovering. You will measure it, then close it, and keep the traces.
evidence: Git history with the dual-write path committed before the outbox table and poller
A captured dual-write run: a domain row exists, the corresponding Kafka consume dump does not contain that event, and the crash/kill point is named
A captured outbox run of the same crash point: the row exists, the event appears after poller recovery, and a retry does not create a second domain effect on the consumer
At least two exported traces (or trace screenshots plus raw JSON) showing the dual-write path breaking after the DB span and the outbox path continuing through poller publish and consumer process
README stating the outbox transaction boundary and the consumer idempotency key
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: The dual-write reproduction leaves a committed PostgreSQL row whose event never appears in a consume of the target topic after the named crash.

The outbox reproduction uses one database transaction for the domain row and the outbox row; after the same crash and a poller restart, the event is consumed exactly once as a domain effect (duplicates allowed on the wire if the consumer is idempotent).
Two traces (or exported spans) are submitted: one ends after the DB write with no publish span; one includes commit, outbox poll, publish, and consumer handling for the same business id.
README names the idempotency key the consumer uses and states that the pipeline is at-least-once plus idempotence, not broker exactly-once.
